title: 15-minute-prep-one-on-one-cheat-sheet
content:
Purpose: quick, repeatable template for really short 1:1s (15 min). Focus on: 1) unblock removal 2) a single progress highlight 3) one ask or decision. Use as pre-read and then take tiny scribbled notes during the meeting.

Structure (strict 15m):
- 0:00-1:00: Quick check-in (1 line) - mood + any major blocker.
- 1:00-5:00: Win / progress highlight (focus on impact, not tasks).
- 5:00-10:00: Single ask or decision item (present context, options, recommended next step).
- 10:00-13:00: Manager feedback / quick coaching (one micro-skill to practice).
- 13:00-15:00: Confirm actions, owners, calendar/next steps.

What I fill before the 1:1 (2–3 min):
- Quick status line: "On track / at risk / blocked" + one-sentence reason.
  Example: "At risk: cross-functional runway for People Ops hiring plan — pending budget sign-off from Finance."
- 1-line highlight (impact): "Reduced new-hire onboarding time from 8 days -> 5 days by consolidating first-week docs; estimated 20% lower follow-up tickets."
- Single ask (concrete): "Can you unblock budget approval for Q2 contractor (people-ops recruiter) so we can start interviews by 3/22? Option A: approve $18k; Option B: reallocate hiring credit from Platform Eng."
- Top feedback question (optional): "Do you think I'm delegating enough of recurring logistics?"

Preparation cues (notes to self):
- Data points to bring: # of open reqs, avg time-to-offer, onboarding NPS (if any), ticket counts. Keep numbers rounded.
- Evidence examples (1–2 small anecdotes): "Hired Claire last month; first-week questions fell by 40% after doc changes (support tickets down from 25->15)."
- Risks to call out succinctly: budget delay, too many simultaneous hires, single person dependency for vendor setup.

Script crib (first 90s):
"Quick status: on track for Q1 OKR M2, but hitting a budget gating issue for contractor hires (reason). Highlight: onboarding friction fix reduced follow-ups and speeds ramp. Ask: recommend we reallocate one hiring credit or approve $18k — I recommend approve to keep schedule. Any immediate thoughts?"

Common manager asks I should be ready for (prep answers):
- "What happens if budget is delayed by 2 weeks?" -> "We can shift non-critical reqs, but slow hiring will push project X 3 weeks; I can reprioritize and pull a temp recruiter for 4 weeks at lower scope."
- "How will we measure success?" -> "Key signals: time-to-productive (days), new-hire-help tickets in week 1, hiring funnel conversion rate."
- "Can you run this without extra headcount?" -> "Short-term yes at expense of project depth; longer-term no — burnout risk."

Micro feedback ask (2 options):
- Coaching ask A: "One thing I want feedback on this week: clarity of prioritization when I escalate — did I present tradeoffs clearly?"
- Coaching ask B: "One habit to try: two-sentence status in async updates; want your view on whether this is noticeable."

Action log template (to fill during meeting):
- Action 1: [owner] [due date] [quick acceptance criteria]
- Action 2: [owner] [due date] [quick acceptance criteria]
Example: Action 1: Get budget sign-off. Owner: Manager. Due: 2026-03-15. Acceptance: email thread with explicit approval or reallocation plan.

Quick self-rating (one line, 1–5) + why: 
- Execution: 4 — shipped onboarding docs, delivered initial metrics.
- Influence: 3 — correlations made, but need more stakeholder nudges for Finance.

Raw scratchbox (used during call):
- Notes on manager reactions / exact phrases.
- Follow-ups promised by manager (copy email or ticket id).
- Any soft commitments (e.g., "I'll try to push Finance") -> write date + context.

Post-1:1 immediate micro-steps (5 min after):
1) Update the action log in this doc.
2) Create the Linear ticket or update existing one with manager quote + requested deliverable.
3) Send 1-line summary to manager as follow-up (cc stakeholders if asked).

Example follow-up message (one line):
"Thanks — filing budget approval action: Manager to confirm by 3/15; I'll prepare the recruiter JD and interview panel list by 3/18."

Personal stretch experiment (quarterly): choose one small thing to try for growth — track for 6 weeks.
- Current: run 2 stakeholder 15-min syncs/week to accelerate Finance approvals. Hypothesis: 2x faster turnaround on budget-related decisions.

Notes to self (messy):
- Keep this doc short. If I predict >2 asks, schedule a longer 30-min sync.
- If manager gives vague advice, ask for a specific next-step or timeline (force specificity).
- Bring one example of a win + one tiny data point (numbers matter).

End of doc — use as living cheat-sheet. When it gets longer than a page, split into quarterly review doc.
